title: Research Army
summary: Get a research post on your niche: an army of Haiku 5.5 agents and one Opus 5.5 race to research the most-liked recent Threads posts in your niche with the same brief and Read-only tools; a script checks every claim; Threadify writes the post from the winner's backed findings and schedules it after one yes. Free; the corpus uses your own ScrapeCreators credits.
triggers: get a research post on my niche
write a research post about my niche
what do the most liked threads posts in my niche have in common

inputs.name: the owner's niche (from the Threadify Brain, confirmed in one line), the owner's own ScrapeCreators API key, the claude command line (Claude Code) on this computer, optional Threadify connection and offer for the post

outputs.name: research-army/<date>/ folder with keywords.json, raw searches, corpus.json (honestly labelled), the race brief and run logs, findings-army.json, findings-opus.json, check.json, a local scoreboard.html and post.md, and optionally one scheduled post with its readback

free_capabilities: corpus builder for ScrapeCreators Threads keyword searches: last-30-days window, dedupe, simple English filter, top 100 by likes, an honest label and credit readback before and after
one-time ScrapeCreators key setup that keeps the key out of chat, command lines and outputs
a fair race of headless Claude Code runs: same brief, Read-only tools, Bash not offered and denied, and a Bash audit from each run's own log
a two-round Haiku army (scouts nominate, commander picks 8, every scout counts, commander sums) against one Opus, with a live two-lane terminal view
a deterministic claim checker with a fixed catalog of machine-checkable tests, exact and within-1 verdicts and example-quote checks
winner rule (backed claims, then cost, then time), a terminal scoreboard and a local HTML scoreboard
local editable post block with a Done editing button
local casing guard that proves lower(original) == lower(final) for the post
paid_capability_stubs: the corpus uses about 25-30 credits of the owner's own ScrapeCreators account
the race uses the owner's own Claude plan (a few cents to about a dollar of model time)
optional Threadify post generation counts toward the plan's AI generations

must_show: the exact final post text and any tracked link
action: schedule this post; nothing publishes now

instructions: Never print, repeat or put the ScrapeCreators API key in a command line; only scrapecreators-key.mjs save writes it.
Show the credit estimate before pulling; stop at 40 credits; never buy credits for the owner.
Label the corpus exactly as the script does; never say most viewed or top on Threads.
Never give either side Bash or code tools; if the Bash audit is not clean, say the race was not fair.
Never change the brief, prompts or catalog to favour either side.
When a side fails or is stopped, count its claims as unbacked and say so.
Use only the winner's backed findings and the checker's numbers in the post.
Never write the post yourself when Threadify generation is unavailable; stop after the scoreboard.
Never call publish_now; schedule only after the owner's exact yes to the post card, and read the schedule back.
When a schedule outcome is unclear, read back before retrying and retry only with the same idempotency key.

must_prove: corpus label, counts and ScrapeCreators credits before and after
brief sha256 shared by both sides
Bash audit for both sides (offered and used)
scoreboard: backed claims (exact and within 1), cost and wall time per side
winner and the rule that decided it
post: model, facts used, editor receipt or unchanged, casing guard
approval reply, scheduled slot and readback
